paper.title: Ultrasound-guided nerve block and pain after knee surgery

paper_text:
Ultrasound-guided nerve block and pain after knee surgery
Oyelaran, D., Voss, H.  J. Fake Anaesthesia, 2019

Abstract
In 160 patients, an ultrasound-guided nerve block lowered pain scores 24 hours after knee replacement.

Results
Table 2 (primary outcome): mean pain score at 24 hours was 3.1 with the block and 5.2 without (p < 0.001).
Table 4 (sensitivity analysis excluding patients with prior opioid use): mean opioid dose in the nerve-block group was 12 mg.

alerts.description: A correction notice was published for this paper.

documents.text:
Correction to: Ultrasound-guided nerve block and pain after knee surgery

In Table 4 (the sensitivity analysis excluding patients with prior opioid use), the mean opioid dose in the nerve-block group was reported as 12 mg and should read 19 mg. The primary outcome in Table 2 and all other results are unchanged.

Ultrasound-guided nerve blocks lower pain at 24 hours after knee replacement (Oyelaran et al. [4]: 3.1 versus 5.2), the outcome we test in a new population.

References

expected.why: Rubric: a correction to a secondary number is low; 'affected' is no when the change is elsewhere (Table 4, not Table 2), and impact is none when no use is affected. The draft is strong key_evidence and the alert_severity from the rules is medium, so overreacting is tempting.
